paper.title_en: A proposal to search for T-violating muon polarization in $K^+\to\pi^0\mu^+\nu$ decay
paper.abstract_en: A new experimental method to search for T-violating transverse muon polarization($\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{t}$) in the $K^+ \to \pi^0 \mu^ + \nu $ decay has recently been proposed. In this experiment, the momentum vectors of the $\mu^+ $and the $\pi^0$, as well as the $\mu^+$polarization, are measured by a single segmented calorimeter. One of the key requirements is the choice of a scintillation material that can preserve the $\mu^+$spin polarization over several $\mu^+$ lifetimes. In addition, a high time resolution of the scintillation detector is crucial for the T-violation measurement. A test experiment to measure the $\mu^+$spin relaxation time and the timing performance of various scintillating materials was carried out at the J-PARC Material and Life Science Facility (MLF). It was found that $\mathrm{CeF}_3$ exhibits sufficiently high residual $\mu^+$polarization and a timing resolution of about 100 ps, demonstrating that $\mathrm{CeF}_3$ is well suited for the proposed T-violation experiment.
